D021-D016_h001.question: "It's been… tough, lately. For a good six months now. I’m a nurse, you know, on the psych ward, so I see a lot, but this... it feels different when it’s you. My ex-husband, he always said I was too hard on myself, and maybe he was right. My plate at dinner, it’s mostly just salad, maybe some grilled chicken. I really watch what I eat. Some things, like bread or anything with a lot of sugar, I just can’t bring myself to touch them. I know it sounds silly but it feels like if I even look at a slice of cake, I'll gain five pounds instantly. I’ve lost a bit of weight, and I really don’t want to put it back on. My scrubs feel looser, which is… good, I suppose, though my doctor keeps harping on my BMI. And the food thing… it’s always on my mind. What I can or can’t eat, how much, when. It just cycles through my head all the time."
D021-D016_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h001.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h002.question: It’s been about six months now, maybe a little more, since I really started noticing things. I own my own jewelry shop, and for years, I've always been so particular about everything – the displays, the inventory, especially my own appearance. Lately, though, it feels like it’s gone beyond that. I find myself just… skipping meals. Sometimes it’s breakfast because I’m so focused on checking stock, other times it’s lunch, and then dinner just feels unimportant. My husband notices, of course, and he's worried because I've just been steadily losing weight. The scale is a constant presence in my mind. I weigh myself every morning, sometimes several times, and even a tiny fluctuation sends me into a panic. Then there’s the food itself – I spend so much time planning what I *might* eat, or arranging it in a certain way, that by the time I could actually eat, I just lose my appetite. It feels like I’m trapped in this cycle, always thinking about my weight or whether I’ve had "too much," even when I haven’t had much at all.
D021-D016_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h002.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h003.question: "It’s been rough lately, Doc. I’m usually strong, you know, with the construction work and all, but my energy’s just gone. I’m 36, single, and honestly, the thought of eating a full meal scares me sometimes. I’ve dropped a good twenty pounds over the past few months. I look at certain foods, especially anything with carbs or, God forbid, fat, and I just see myself blowing up. I mean, I’ve got to stay agile for the job, right? I try to stick to a very strict list of 'safe' foods, mostly just lean protein and some greens, but even then, I worry. I’ve started thinking about food a lot more than I used to, too – like, what I’m eating, when, how much. It's almost constant. Sometimes I find myself washing my hands over and over before I even touch my plate, or checking labels repeatedly even if I know what's in it. I don't know why, it just feels like I have to. It's exhausting."
D021-D016_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h003.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h004.question: It’s been a rough few months, doc. Out at sea, the routine keeps me busy, but when I’m home, things get… muddled. My wife, she’s noticed I’ve been skipping meals more often. Says I’m not eating enough, especially breakfast or a proper dinner. It's just... I watch the scales, you know? Every morning, and if that number nudges up, even a pound, it just throws me. I start thinking about how I need to get it back down, even though I'm already lighter than I used to be. It’s like a constant hum in my head. Before I eat, I’ll get these thoughts, and I end up cutting out certain things, or making sure I don’t eat too much. I try not to let it show, but it’s always there, this… focus, on what I’m eating, or not eating.
D021-D016_h004.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h004.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h005.question: It’s hard to pinpoint when it all started, but for the past six months or so, food has just… taken over. As a chef, that sounds ironic, right? But I find myself meticulously planning every single thing I eat, right down to the calorie. I’ve cut out so many ingredients I used to love working with, convinced they’ll make me instantly put on weight. Even though my wife says I'm looking too thin, I still feel like I need to drop more. It’s like there’s this constant hum in my head, a loop about food. I'll spend hours researching recipes, not to cook for the restaurant, but to find the absolute "safest" things to prepare for myself, constantly checking and re-checking every detail. And if I feel like I've eaten something "wrong," I get an overwhelming urge to go for a run, even if it's late at night.
D021-D016_h005.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D021-D016_h005.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h006.question:
It’s hard to pinpoint exactly when things started feeling this…unsettled. I’ve always been quite meticulous, especially with my PhD thesis, but lately, it’s spilled over into everything. I’ve cut out almost all carbs and fats, though I try to balance it with other things, you know, to stay healthy. I’ve lost a bit of weight, and some people have commented, but I feel fine, honestly. Just trying to be careful. My research is so demanding; I can’t afford to feel sluggish.

The thing is, food has become this…project. I find myself constantly thinking about what I’m going to eat, if it’s "right," if I've checked all the labels. Sometimes I replay an interaction in my head, wondering if I ate too much or the wrong thing, even if it was just a small snack. It’s exhausting. And if dinner plans change last minute, or I can't find a very specific brand of something, I feel completely thrown off. It’s been going on for a few months now, and while I wouldn’t say it’s impacting my work, it’s certainly taking up a lot of mental space. I just want to feel normal again, like I can just eat a meal without mentally dissecting it.
D021-D016_h006.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D016_h006.answer: A & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h007.question:
It's been a tough few months, probably since the divorce was finalized. I used to enjoy cooking, but now I find myself really scrutinizing everything I eat. I’ve cut out all carbs and most fats – it just feels… safer. I know I’ve lost a bit of weight, and my doctor has mentioned it, but I honestly don't think it's a big deal. I feel fine. My ex always said I was too emotional, so perhaps this is just my way of taking control.

The strangest thing is how much I think about food. It's not about being hungry or enjoying a meal. It's more about calculating, planning, almost like a compulsion to make sure I stick to my very limited list of "safe" foods. If I deviate, even a little, I feel incredibly anxious, almost panicked. I'll re-read labels over and over, just to be sure. It takes up so much of my mental energy. I can't shake these thoughts about food, even when I'm trying to focus on work or relaxing. It’s exhausting, and I just want it to stop.
D021-D016_h007.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D016_h007.answer: A & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h008.question: I’m not really sure why I’m here. My husband, David, insisted. He thinks I’m not eating enough, but I just… I’m careful about what I consume. I teach piano all day, and I need to be light on my feet, have a clear head. I stick to around 800 calories most days. It’s been like this for about six months now. I used to be heavier, and I just felt so sluggish. The weight has naturally been coming off, and I feel better when my clothes fit looser. David worries when I get dizzy sometimes, especially during lessons, but it’s probably just because I’m busy. My periods have been a bit irregular too, but honestly, it’s one less thing to worry about. Sometimes I find myself thinking about what I’ll eat all day, planning it out, making sure it’s just right. It’s hard to focus on other things when those thoughts get stuck.
D021-D016_h008.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D016_h008.answer: A & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h009.question: I’m not really sure why I’m here, to be honest. My sister practically dragged me. She and my doctor seem to think something’s wrong because I’ve lost a bit of weight, but I really don’t see the big deal. I’ve just been, you know, watching what I eat. It’s not much, usually just a few bites at meals, or sometimes I’ll skip dinner entirely if I’m really busy with work. A content marketer’s schedule can be pretty demanding, and I just don’t have time to worry about every single meal. Plus, I’ve always been a bit particular about things, and now it just feels like the right way to manage my intake. I’ve dropped a few sizes over the past few months, and honestly, I just feel a bit lighter, that's all. Everyone’s just overreacting.
D021-D016_h009.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D016_h009.answer: A & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h010.question: "It’s been a rough few months, doc. My wife, bless her heart, keeps trying to get me to eat more, but honestly, food just… it's a lot. I've found myself skipping meals more often than not, especially breakfast and lunch, trying to, you know, just streamline things. The guys at the factory have noticed too, asking if I'm feeling alright. I just tell them I'm fine, trying to get in shape, but they worry too much. It’s not a big deal. My weight’s been going down, steadily, for over six months now. Everyone just makes such a fuss about it. I have to admit, I do think about food quite a bit, about what I'm going to eat, or more often, what I'm *not* going to eat, and how that affects my day. Sometimes I'll even re-arrange things on my plate several times before I even consider taking a bite. It feels... important."
D021-D016_h010.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D016_h010.answer: A & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h011.question: I’m not really sure why I’m here, to be honest. My ex-wife kept hounding me to see someone, said I’ve been different since the divorce about six months ago. She thinks I’m not eating enough. I’ve just been really focused on my work, you know? And yeah, I've cut out a lot of carbs and fats. It’s not a big deal, I just feel… cleaner, I guess. I spend a lot of time thinking about what I’m going to eat, and if it’s "right." I’ve dropped a few pounds, maybe a stone or two. It’s hard not to notice, and honestly, when I’m at a good weight, I feel like I'm more on top of things, more capable. Everything seems to click into place, even on set. If my weight is off, I just feel… less. It just feels important to keep control over that, you know?

A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D021-D016_h011.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h012.question: "It's been a rough few months, doc. My wife, bless her heart, says I’m wasting away, and I can see it too, with my uniform getting looser. I’ve just been cutting back more and more, trying to be really careful about what I eat, just a few hundred calories a day. I look in the mirror and still see this big gut staring back, especially around my middle, even though everyone says I'm thin. I can't seem to stop losing weight. The thing is, I find myself thinking about food almost constantly, what I ate, what I will eat, if I’ve had too much. I check and recheck online guides about healthy eating, weighing every little thing. It's like a loop in my head, can’t get it to stop."
D021-D016_h012.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D021-D016_h012.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h013.question: It's been… I don't know, a good six months now, maybe more. I just started really watching what I eat. With my job, the stress is immense, and frankly, I need to be sharp. I started cutting things out, little by little, to feel more in control. Now, I barely eat anything, just enough to get through the day, maybe a small salad or some fruit. I’ve definitely lost weight – my clothes are all so loose, and people are starting to comment, which is annoying. I look in the mirror and I still see… softness, and I just can’t stand it. A few pounds off here, a few pounds off there, and maybe I’ll finally feel okay. I spend a lot of time thinking about what I’m going to eat, or rather, not eat. It's like a constant mental battle, planning out every morsel, making sure I don’t mess up my routine. If I eat something "bad," I just feel disgusted and it’s all I can think about. Sometimes, if I feel like I've deviated, I spend hours reading articles about healthy eating, researching every ingredient, just to get back on track.
D021-D016_h013.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D021-D016_h013.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h014.question:
"It's been a tough few months, probably since the divorce was finalized, if I'm honest. I've found myself just… losing interest in food. Skipping meals, especially breakfast and lunch, has become a habit. I tell myself I'm busy, that I don't need it, even though I'm clearly much leaner than I used to be. But when I look in the mirror, all I see is this extra bulk, especially around my stomach. I just want to shed a few more pounds, feel lighter, more in control.

I started getting these nagging thoughts, especially around meal times. I’ll spend ages checking labels, calculating, recounting. If I don't follow my own twisted rules, I get this intense anxiety, like something bad will happen. It’s exhausting, constantly fighting with my own head about what I can or can’t eat. It's like I have to do these things, or I can't move on with my day. It's really affecting my focus on set, and that's never happened before."
D021-D016_h014.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D021-D016_h014.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h015.question:
"Well, lately, things have been… off. It’s hard to put a finger on it, but for about eight months now, I’ve just not felt myself. My wife, bless her heart, keeps telling me I’m getting too thin. And she’s right, the weight just keeps dropping off, even though I’m not really trying to lose it, not exactly anyway. I’ve started skipping meals, mostly breakfast and sometimes lunch, just because I get caught up in things.

It's strange, but I find myself spending a lot of time thinking about food. Not in a hungry way, more like… I get these thoughts stuck in my head, about what I should or shouldn't eat, and how things should be prepared. If something's not quite right, it can really throw me off for the rest of the day. And honestly, it makes me feel like a failure if I don't stick to these invisible rules I've made for myself, especially when it comes to my weight. It's like my whole day, my whole sense of being a decent person, hinges on that number on the scale."
D021-D016_h015.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D021-D016_h015.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h016.question:
"It's been a rough few months, doc, maybe even closer to half a year. Ever since the divorce, things just… shifted. Being on the road, it’s easy to get into bad habits, but I’ve been trying to keep myself in line. I’ve cut out a lot of stuff – no more sugary drinks, no carbs, definitely no fatty foods. I feel like if I eat something 'bad,' it'll just blow me up overnight, you know?

My ex always used to tease me about putting on weight, so I've been pretty strict. My clothes are looser, but I still feel like I could lose a few more pounds. The problem is, sometimes I just can't get that thought out of my head – what if I ate something I shouldn’t have? I’ll spend hours thinking about whether I really cleaned my plate enough, or if there’s some hidden ingredient in the protein bar I just had. It's exhausting, and honestly, it’s getting in the way of getting decent sleep when I’m trying to make my runs."
D021-D016_h016.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D016_h016.answer: D & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D021-D016_h017.question: I’m not really sure why I’m here, honestly. My husband sort of insisted. Things have been… a little off, I guess, for the past six months or so. D021-D016_h021.question: "It's been... I don't know, a few months now, maybe since the start of the semester, that things just feel off.
